text.en:
MALACAÑAN PALACE
BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE PHILIPPINES
[ EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 130, November 28, 1937 ]
AMENDING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 61, DATED NOVEMBER 3, 1936, ENTITLED “CREATING A
NATIONAL RELIEF BOARD,” SO AS TO DESIGNATE THE COMMISSIONER OF HEALTH AND
WELFARE AS MEMBER AND EXECUTIVE OFFICER OF SAID BOARD
Executive Order Numbered Sixty-one, dated November third, nineteen hundred and thirty-six, entitled
“Creating a National Relief Board,” is hereby amended to read as follows:
“For the purpose of carrying out the provisions of Commonwealth Act Numbered Ninety, approved October
twenty-sixth, nineteen hundred and thirty-six, entitled “An Act to appropriate the sum of one million five
hundred thousand pesos for relief and rehabilitation work in the different provinces devastated by typhoons,
floods, or other public calamities,” there is hereby created a National Relief Board to be composed of the
Secretary of the Interior as Chairman, the Commissioner of the Budget, the Commissioner of Health and
Welfare, the Deputy Chief of Staff of the Philippine Army, the Director of Public Welfare, the Director Public
Works, the Director of Health, the Director of Education, and the Director of Plant Industry, as members. In
the absence of any of the members, the Department Head concerned may designate another officer to take his
place in the Board. The Commissioner of Health and Welfare shall be the Executive Officer of the Board. The
Board may employ such personnel as the President may authorize.
“This Board shall investigate the extent of the damages caused by the typhoons, floods, and other public
calamities in the different provinces, determine the amounts needed for relief and rehabilitation work, and,
subject to the approval of the President, allot the necessary funds therefore from the appropriation made under
Commonwealth Act Numbered Ninety for expenditure through such government agencies or charitable
institutions as it may designate.
“All officers and employees of the Departments, Bureaus, offices, agencies, and instrumentalities of the
National Government and those of the provinces, cities, municipalities, and other political subdivisions as well
as those of the institutions receiving financial aid from the Government, are hereby enjoined to cooperate with
the Board in the performance of its functions and, with the approval of the corresponding Head of
Department, shall, when necessary, render such service as the Board or any of its members may assign to
“All expenses which may be incurred by the Board to carry out the provisions of this Executive Order,
including traveling and other incidental expenses of any of its members and of the officers and employees
rendering relief work under the said Board, shall be a proper charge against the appropriation authorized by
Commonwealth Act Numbered Ninety.
“To assist the National Relief Board in its work, there is hereby created in each province a provincial relief
board to be composed of the provincial governor, as chairman, the provincial treasurer, the district engineer,
the district health officer, the division superintendent of schools, the provincial agricultural supervisor, and the
military provincial commander, as members, whose duty it shall be to conduct on the field a preliminary
investigation of the extent of the damages caused by the typhoons, floods, and other public calamities, make
an appraisal of the extent of such damages, and recommend to the National Relief Board the nature of the
needed relief and rehabilitation work and the amount of funds necessary to carry out such work.”
